messages.summary:
## Objective
- Upgrade the existing Neon Mile racing game with more modern-looking cars and graphics while keeping its retro feel.
- Add meaningful driving physics, varied hazards, collision damage and paid repairs, and more routes.

## Requirements
- Implement a complete, playable game change without asking clarifying questions.
- Include acceleration, deceleration, cornering speed loss, road bumps, collision speed loss, hard-impact damage and reduced maximum speed, additional obstacles, repair costs after races, and more maps.

## Decisions
- Added two routes, with level-based unlocks defined in a shared `unlockLevels` array.
- Modeled vehicle damage as persistent per-car state, with a repair bill of 22 coins per damage point, deducted from race rewards and remaining coins.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Neon City Bypass and Canyon Run routes.
- Added per-car damage state, speed/handling physics variables, braking state, and expanded obstacle spawning with bumps, oil, debris, and barriers.
- Added collision-based damage and speed loss, repair-cost deduction, and repair information in the result summary.
- Updated route unlock checks and route count display.

### Active
- Finish integrating and validating the physics, damage, repair, and route changes; the edits to `game.js` are incomplete.
- Improve modern car and scene graphics, and ensure the new hazards render correctly.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` for consistency and runtime errors, especially `finishRace()` repair/reward accounting and the race HUD.
2. Update controls for braking and make HUD reflect actual speed, boost, and damage; update route-dependent UI and tips.
3. Improve car and road rendering, including visible impact damage and distinct hazard artwork.
4. Run the game in a browser, play through a route, and verify collisions, persistent damage, repair payment, and route unlocks.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing game implementation and all changes so far.
- `index.html`: Race HUD, canvas, route and garage UI.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests or browser verification have been run.
- `game.js` was only partially updated. In particular, rendering still uses the original car/obstacle art; `drawRaceHud()` still computes speed using the old formula; controls currently do not set `braking`; and route cycling still uses the old four-route unlock logic.
- The user requested screenshots for checks: save small JPEGs (viewport at most 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest one.

## Objective
- Upgrade Neon Mile into a complete, playable racer with modern-looking cars and graphics that retain a retro feel.
- Add meaningful driving physics, hazards, collision damage and paid repairs, and more routes.

## Requirements
- Implement acceleration, deceleration, cornering speed loss, road bumps, collision speed loss, hard-impact damage and reduced maximum speed.
- Add more obstacles, repair costs after races, and more maps.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Added two routes, with unlock levels stored in a shared `unlockLevels` array.
- Damage persists per car; repairs cost 22 coins per damage point and are settled after races.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Neon City Bypass and Canyon Run routes.
- Added per-car damage state, initial acceleration/braking/cornering physics, boost use, and obstacle spawning for bumps, oil, debris, barriers, and other hazards.
- Added collision-based damage and speed loss, repair settlement, and repair information in the result summary.
- Updated route unlock checks and route count display.
- Updated the race distance UI to use a dynamic `raceDistance` element.

### Active
- Validate and fix the partially integrated `game.js` physics, collision, repair/reward accounting, and race HUD.
- Wire braking controls and update route cycling to use `unlockLevels`.
- Improve modern car and road rendering, visible impact damage, and distinct hazard artwork.
- Verify gameplay, collisions, persistent damage, repair payments, and route unlocks in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Inspect `finishRace()` accounting and update the HUD to show actual speed, boost, and damage.
2. Add braking controls and fix the route cycling logic; update route-dependent UI and tips.
3. Improve car, road, and hazard graphics, including visible damage and bump feedback.
4. Run the game in a browser and verify a race end-to-end; capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Route data, physics, obstacles, race completion and rendering.
- `index.html`: Garage, route UI, race HUD, canvas, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Existing visual styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests or browser verification have been run.
- `game.js` still has legacy obstacle and car artwork; `drawRaceHud()` uses a hard-coded speed formula; `braking` is declared but not wired to controls; route cycling still references the old unlock-level array.
- The active race HUD now references `<span id="raceDistance">` for its route distance.
